Ontology_AssayAndWorkflow_prompt.notes: The experiment focuses on XL-MS and q-XL-MS to study the interaction between FAT10 and the SUMO E1 enzyme (AOS1/UBA2). While the study discusses SUMOylation and FAT10ylation, the actual mass spectrometry runs described are for chemical crosslinking analysis, not PTM-enrichment (like diGly or QQTGG) of the proteome.

Ontology_SampleSourceAndScope_prompt.notes: The mass spectrometry analysis (XL-MS and q-XL-MS) was performed on purified recombinant proteins (AOS1/UBA2, FAT10, SUMO-1) expressed in E. coli, not on whole cell lysates. Ontology_TreatmentAndDesign_prompt.notes: The proteomics analysis specifically refers to the XL-MS and q-XL-MS experiments described in the PRIDE metadata and the 'Chemical crosslinking coupled to mass spectrometry' section. While the paper describes many cell-based assays (IFN-gamma/TNF-alpha stimulation, CRISPR KO), the MS data is focused on the in vitro interaction between the SUMO E1 enzyme (AOS1/UBA2) and FAT10/SUMO-1.

base_candidates_ranked.reason: Data-dependent acquisition (DDA) on Orbitrap Fusion with MS1 intensity-based quantification (LFQ) for crosslink abundance.

modifier_candidates_ranked.reason: Explicit use of BS3 (H12/D12 BS3) for chemical cross-linking (XL-MS and q-XL-MS).

Ontology_ProcessingAndDifferential_promp.notes: The experiment is a specialized chemical cross-linking (XL-MS) study. Standard bottom-up pipelines will fail to identify the cross-linked peptides without a specialized search engine like xQuest or a cross-link aware search configuration. The differential analysis is focused on the abundance of specific cross-link sites (q-XL-MS).
